If an attorney takes your case, they work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover money. whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Claim

items.title: You Generally Have Two Years
items.desc: California law gives most injury victims two years from the date of the accident to file a claim. That window shrinks to as little as six months if a government entity is involved, so it's worth checking your timeline early.

items.title: Being Partly at Fault Doesn't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you share some blame for the crash, you can still recover damages - just reduced by your percentage of fault.

items.title: No Ceiling on Pain-and-Suffering Damages
items.desc: Unlike some states, California doesn't cap non-economic damages like pain and suffering in typical injury cases, which can matter a lot depending on how the injury affects your life.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Unless You Win
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency. That means there's no upfront fee, and they only get paid if you receive a settlement or award.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in Ripon?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the accident to file a personal injury claim. If a government vehicle or agency was involved, that deadline can shrink to as little as six months, so it's smart to look into your situation sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, so being partly responsible doesn't bar you from recovering compensation. Your recovery would simply be reduced by your share of fault, which an attorney can help evaluate.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Ripon?
items.answer: Public collision records show higher counts along corridors like SR-99, N Jack Tone Road, and W Main Street, with crashes tending to peak on Fridays between 4 and 6 p.m. These are simply reported counts, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and we are not a law firm ourselves. We simply help connect injured people with an independent attorney who may be able to help.

items.question: Will I have to pay an attorney upfront?
items.answer: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover money for you. This lets you get help without worrying about upfront legal costs.
